summary.title: A Template Engine (500 Lines or Less)
summary.one_liner: You learn how a Django-style template engine works by compiling templates into Python functions, using a CodeBuilder helper and the Templite class.
takeaways: Templates keep static markup mostly intact and embed dynamic parts with {{ }}, {% %} and {# #} notation.
Interpretation walks a parsed data structure at render time; compilation turns the template into Python code once, which is faster when rendered many times.
The engine compiles each template into a render_function that builds a list of strings and joins them.
CodeBuilder manages indentation and source lines, and exec() turns the generated source into callable functions.
Dot access, filters, if and for blocks are handled by translating them into Python code and a do_dots helper.
summary.summary: The chapter from the 500 Lines or Less book explains why templates exist: they keep mostly static text separate from dynamic logic, unlike code that embeds strings. It describes the Django-based syntax the engine supports, including variables, dot access, filters, conditionals, loops and comments. It then contrasts interpretation with compilation and explains that this engine compiles templates into Python functions, with micro-optimizations explained. The walkthrough builds the Templite class and a CodeBuilder helper that generates and executes source code.
